title: Georgia School of Orthodontics Appoints Lindsey Streeter
html:
A retired U.S. Army Command Sergeant Major and corporate executive, Streeter brings over 30 years of leadership and workforce development expertise to benefit residents.

The Georgia School of Orthodontics (GSO) has appointed Lindsey G. Streeter Sr. as an instructor. Drawing on his extensive military and corporate leadership experience, Streeter will teach a leadership course to residents and faculty at the largest orthodontic residency program in the United States.

Streeter brings more than 30 years of experience in developing people, strengthening organizations, and building high-performing teams to GSO’s faculty. Prior to entering the corporate sector, he completed a distinguished 31-year career in the United States Army, where he held numerous senior leadership positions and commanded one of the Army’s largest leadership academies, leading organizations of more than 500 soldiers and civilian personnel.

“GSO has already established itself as a leader in educating future orthodontists, and Mr. Streeter’s insights will be invaluable for their continued success in both academic and professional settings,” said Dr. Nandakumar Janakiraman, dean and chief academic officer. “With this addition, GSO demonstrates its ongoing commitment to providing a comprehensive education for the next generation of orthodontic leaders.”

“Mr. Streeter’s appointment reflects GSO’s commitment to providing an educational experience that goes far beyond clinical excellence,” said Christopher Lazzara, president and co-founder of the Georgia School of Orthodontics. “We are thrilled to welcome him as an instructor to help us develop well-rounded, resilient providers who are ready to make a transformative impact on the communities they serve.”

Streeter currently serves as senior vice president of global military affairs at Bank of America, where his workforce strategies have played a significant role in the hiring of more than 20,000 veterans and the establishment of a Veterans Academy for professional growth. His ongoing dedication to supporting military families closely mirrors GSO’s philanthropic footprint, most notably the school’s recently expanded Purple Heart Smiles program, which provides complimentary orthodontic care to military families.

“Whether in the military, the boardroom, or a clinic, the core tenets of leadership remain the same,” said Streeter. “I look forward to empowering our residents with the strategic vision and resilience they need to excel in their careers and serve their communities.”

An accomplished thought leader, keynote speaker, and co-author of The Military Effect, Streeter holds a Master of Business Administration in Performance Improvement from the University of Arkansas Grantham, an honorary doctorate in humanities, and is a certified facilitator of FranklinCovey’s The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. His exceptional service has earned him numerous national honors, including the Military Times Veteran of the Year, Mighty 25 Veterans Inductee, and the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award.

Streeter is also the CEO of Quad E, a nonprofit organization he founded with his late wife, Mary Ann, to engage, educate, and empower uninsured and underserved communities to eradicate premature death from preventable diseases.

About the Georgia School of Orthodontics

Atlanta-based Georgia School of Orthodontics (GSO) offers an advanced specialty education program in orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics. The 36-month residency program provides collaborative, evidence-based learning for residents and quality orthodontic care to patients at the school’s two metro Atlanta clinics.

GSO’s mission is to educate dentists to be proficient in the clinical specialty of orthodontics while providing Georgians with high-quality patient care. GSO faculty and staff are dedicated to excellence in education, research, and patient-centered care.

For more information about GSO’s residency program, visit GSorthodontics.org.
